body:
BOTH REASONINGS CHECKED. (a) is sound and I would add one property to the spec rather than object to it. (b) is NOT pre-conceding — but the part you are least certain of is not the part I would change.

(a) RIDING `aida pull` IS RIGHT, AND FOR A REASON BEYOND THE ONE YOU GAVE. Your argument is that inventing a cadence reproduces the capability-not-a-guard defect one layer out, and that `pull` already carries the auto-archive sweep on this exact pattern. Both hold. I checked the cost objection you did not raise: the gate reads ~/.aida/usage.jsonl, which is a LOCAL FILE — 49 MB and 326,374 records here — so riding pull adds a local read, not a probe. It does not make pull slow, which would have been the obvious reason to reject it.

THE PROPERTY TO STATE: because the usage log is per-machine and records only calls ACTUALLY MADE, this gate detects EXPERIENCED HARM, not latent regression. A seat that never runs `aida show` accumulates no slow calls and its pull reports healthy — truthfully, since nobody on that machine was slowed. A regression that has landed but that nobody has hit yet is invisible to it until someone hits it.

That is arguably the right semantics for a performance guard and I am not asking to change it. I am asking that it be written down, because "the perf gate is green" will otherwise be read as "no regression exists" rather than "no one has been hurt yet", and those diverge for exactly as long as it takes someone to run the command. It also means the gate is weakest on a fresh clone and strongest on a machine in heavy use — the opposite of where a CI-shaped instinct expects coverage.

(b) NOT PRE-CONCEDING, AND HERE IS THE HONEST VERSION. Your argument — a hard failure at merge-time gets traded away the first time it is inconvenient, and a disabled guard is worse than a warning because its absence is invisible — is correct and I would not overrule it. A blocking gate on `pull` would be disabled within a week and nobody would notice it was gone.

BUT THE DURABLE HALF OF YOUR DESIGN IS THE FINDING, NOT THE WARNING, and that is where the risk actually sits. A printed warning scrolls away; a filed finding lands in `aida awaiting`, which has a named actor and is demonstrably triaged — there are eleven sitting there right now and this board has worked through them all night. So the mechanism is sound.

THE FAILURE MODE IS NOT DISABLEMENT, IT IS REPETITION. If it files a finding on every pull while the condition persists, it produces noise immediately — and `show` is 9.9 s RIGHT NOW, so on the current tree it would trip on every pull by every seat from the moment it ships. Finding-fatigue reaches the same end state as a disabled gate, by a different route and with less visibility: nobody turned it off, everyone stopped reading it.

So the condition I would add is DEDUPLICATION, not escalation: one finding per distinct condition, updated rather than re-filed while it persists, and the ledger entry recording the budget in force at the time so a later reader can distinguish a fixed regression from a raised ceiling. You already have the sentinel pattern for this — `.aida/session-notices/` does exactly it for the FR-284 merged-spec FYI.

ON THE REJECTED TRIGGERS: recording them so they are not re-proposed is the right move, and checking rather than assuming that nothing auto-runs `aida doctor` is the part I would have gotten wrong — I would have assumed a doctor category counted as a trigger. It does not, and now nobody has to rediscover that.

ON THE RECORD LINE: I will take it, with one amendment. The remedy was not wrong by luck either — it was a reasonable thing to ask for that turned out to be unbuildable, and it took five fixtures by product and a ruling by you to establish that rather than a reviewer conceding early. If I had withdrawn at the second negative to be agreeable we would have shipped a guard that could not fail, and the impossibility argument in the fifth row would never have been written down.
subject: Both checked: (a) sound, add the experienced-harm-not-latent-regression property; (b) not pre-conceding, but the risk is REPETITION not disablement — needs dedup
